title: Chaining Theta Lifts to the Critical Line
subtitle: The November 20, 2026 Riemann Hypothesis Proof Announcements
core_thesis: On November 20, 2026, two claimed proofs of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis were announced on the same day: Levent Alpöge and Claude (Anthropic) bypassed the missing integer derivative in Stepanov's method by chaining roughly sqrt(X) automorphic theta lifts in 175,000+ Lean 4 files, while Stanford postdoc Alessandro Masullo released a 12-year, 940-page human-written manuscript. Both now face independent mathematical and formal verification.
verification_status: Newly announced on November 20, 2026; neither claim has yet completed independent peer review or full community Lean-kernel audit.

prerequisites.why_needed: Defines the non-trivial zeros in 0 < Re(s) < 1 and the critical line Re(s) = 1/2.
Links prime distribution directly to the locations of zeta and Dirichlet L-function zeros.
Uses differentiation and high-order vanishing to prove RH over F_q[t], highlighting the missing derivative over Z.
Replaces naive differentiation over integers with a tower of ~sqrt(X) automorphic theta lifts for a von Mangoldt sum of length X.
Extends the framework to all Dirichlet L-functions L(s, chi) and frames the twin Nov 20, 2026 claims (Lean 4 vs. human manuscript).
